描述_EN: the roughness of the construction, decoration and glazing suggests that it contained the ashes of a humble person. when associated with the reign name of an emperor the date is unambiguous, but when it is used alone, as in this case, it gives a range of alternative dates. for this object the style and manufacturing techniques suggest three possible dates: 1206, 1266 or 1326 ad. the inscription also contains a date in chinese lunar dating system. the front side of the coffin is incised with the image of a door surrounded by the names of the 'guardian spirits of the four directions': the green dragon of the east, the red bird of the south, the white tiger of the west and the dark warrior of the north, who were meant to protect the deceased in the grave. cremation was not a native chinese tradition, but was introduced to china with the coming of buddhism after the 4th century ad. confucian officials, however, openly rejected cremation, considering the destruction of the body as an evil act against the confucian, and traditionally chinese, value of filial piety. this piece is a ceramic container in the form of a coffin with lid, used to hold the ashes of the deceased. this new practice was first adopted by buddhist monks in monasteries and then gradually extended to lay believers, particularly during the song period (960-1279).
描述_ZN: 从结构、装饰和釉面的粗糙程度来看，它装的是一个卑微的人的骨灰。 当与一个皇帝的名字联系在一起时，日期是明确的，但当它单独使用时，如在本例中，它提供了一个可供选择的日期范围。 对于这件物品，其风格和制造技术表明了三种可能的日期： 1206年、1266年或公元1326年。 该碑文还包含了中国农历年代系统中的一个日期。 棺材的正面刻有一个门的图像，周围有 "四方守护神 "的名字：东方的青龙、南方的红鸟、西方的白虎和北方的黑武士，他们要在坟墓里保护死者。 火葬不是中国本土的传统，而是在公元4世纪后随着佛教的传入而传入中国。 然而，儒家官员公开反对火葬，认为销毁尸体是违反儒家和中国传统的孝道价值观的邪恶行为。 这件作品是一个带盖的棺材形式的陶瓷容器，用来装死者的骨灰。 这种新的做法首先被寺院里的佛教僧侣采用，然后逐渐扩展到非宗教人士，特别是在宋代（960-1279）。
